description:
We’re a team of students led by an AWS engineer who builds data centers.

Astronauts on Mars can’t just open YouTube and instantly stream videos from Earth. We’re building “YouTube for Mars” to support crew wellbeing, ease isolation through a sense of connection to home, and provide fast offline access to health tutorials in emergencies. Join us to build a working prototype!
summary: Long missions isolate astronauts from Earth and strain wellbeing. ReefyMars combines video journaling, on-device AI expression cues and calming Earth videos to support reflection and connection with home. Inspired by NASA research, it explores future mood and behavior tracking while keeping all processing local because Mars-Earth communication links are slow and intermittent.
details:
Why ReefyMars

Long missions separate crews from Earth, familiar places and everyday support. ReefyMars combines a personal video journal, local AI expression cues and a small Earth-video collection to make reflection and connection with home part of a simple daily routine. It is a student research prototype for the Health Monitoring Software challenge.

Working prototype

Try the live ReefyMars prototype

  • Live camera vlog with person segmentation and a Mars habitat overlay.
  • On-device facial-movement analysis, including smiling, neutral and other visible-expression cues, shown below the person.
  • Local recording with optional microphone audio, Share/save and return to the live view.
  • Three nature videos that play beside the vlog, with optional video fullscreen.
  • A clearly labeled synthetic seven-sol trend that demonstrates a future monitoring interface. It is not measured mood data.

Research and intended impact

NASA behavioral-health research identifies isolation, recreation, connection with home and crew self-report as relevant to wellbeing. The Astronaut Journals Study describes Earth viewing and shared movies as important leisure activities. Published clinical research also links automated facial and vocal observations with depression severity and treatment response. These findings motivate our approach; they do not validate ReefyMars as a medical assessment.

Our aim is to help crews notice changes over time and inform future medical support while keeping personal observations under crew control. Expression is one behavioral signal, not a direct measurement of mood.

Why local matters

Limited by the speed of light, Mars-Earth signals take about 3-22 minutes one way, and communication links are intermittent. AI inference therefore runs on the user's device. The model runtime, model files and video assets are bundled for local hosting; the current web demo still needs an initial page load. At Reefy, our goal is fully offline provisioning and autonomous habitat IT, with automated startup, health checks, recovery and synchronization. Local habitat networks could grow into a Mars internet. Future cargo and return missions could carry bulk datasets on physical storage.

Technology

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Google MediaPipe handles local person segmentation and facial-movement analysis; simple rules produce expression labels. Reefy.ai OS is our platform for offline deployment and management of habitat AI services.

Next steps

We plan opt-in local session summaries, voluntary wellbeing check-ins and personal trends, followed by research into voice and journal text alongside facial observations. Clinical collaboration, consent and validation across users and conditions would be needed before medical use. We have not measured whether the video breaks improve wellbeing.

SI use and credits

ChatGPT/Codex assisted with research, coding, writing and editing. Image generation produced the fictional portrait, scene reconstruction and thumbnail artwork. Trends are synthetic; student footage and narration are original. Full sources, licenses and AI disclosure are in the repository.

Source and documentation: https://github.com/reefyai/reefy-mars
Live demo: https://reefy-mars.aospan.chatgpt.site/
